dimensions.name: Knowledge Delta
dimensions.justification: Provides several expert heuristics (e.g., ALWAYS ENABLE compute environment, BEST_FIT_PROGRESSIVE recommendation, dependency graph) that a baseline model would not state, but the majority of the content restates standard AWS Batch documentation without novel decision trees or thresholds.

dimensions.name: Mindset + Appropriate Procedures
dimensions.justification: Lists AWS‑specific step order (compute‑environment type → allocation strategy → launch template → instance role → subnets → job queue → job definition, etc.) which is concrete, yet many procedures are generic "verify" checks rather than a tightly scoped AWS‑only workflow.

dimensions.name: Anti-Pattern Quality
dimensions.justification: Provides a concrete NEVER list with clear reasoning (e.g., never leave CE DISABLED, never use BEST_FIT for heterogeneous pools). Missing some common pitfalls such as least‑privilege IAM policies and cost‑allocation tagging, so not perfect.

dimensions.name: Specification Compliance
dimensions.justification: Frontmatter is complete, description, keywords, triggers, and output contract are clearly defined. The only shortfall is that the trigger list is long and could cause false positives, but activation criteria are still usable.

dimensions.name: Progressive Disclosure
dimensions.justification: Uses navigation table and layered sections, but front‑loads large tables and full command examples, creating some cognitive overload before the core checklist.

dimensions.name: Freedom Calibration
dimensions.justification: Appropriately tightens constraints for provisioning (prerequisite checks, ENABLED state) while allowing flexibility in optional fields. No over‑constraining of creative tasks.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.justification: Follows a recognizable pattern (Mindset, Heuristics, NEVER list, Output format). Minor ad‑hoc ordering of sections prevents a perfect score.

dimensions.name: Practical Usability
dimensions.justification: Model output examples violate the skill's own contract: they emit READY_TO_DEPLOY even when required items (job definition, CloudWatch metrics) are missing, showing the skill does not reliably enforce prerequisite checks. Missing guidance on how to auto‑detect those gaps reduces real‑world executability.
